text:
maya: quick sync: product wants per-project quotas when a central service account mints tokens for many projects. right now billing attributes to the SA owner org only. how do we map/verify origin project so router and billing can use it?
aj: do we treat this as an asserted claim from our minting service, or derive heuristically from request metadata?
sam: asserted preferred. infra team mints tokens via our internal API; we can add a claim like `x_project` at mint time. router would prefer that when present.
liam: proposed enforcement: request carries either (A) api_key/project header, (B) JWT with x_project, or (C) opaque token + introspect. precedence: 1) trusted x_project, 2) explicit api_key.project, 3) fallback to SA owner.
maya: security caveat: only accept x_project if token signature = our mint-service and iss in allowlist. explainable in console.
aj: what about third-party OIDC tokens? If upstream issues JWT, we should only accept external claims if we've mapped the issuer to a trust relationship and stored a mapping. otherwise reject or require introspect.
rachel: console requirements: 1) when viewing a project's billing page, show both "direct" and "attributed" usage with a toggle. 2) mark rows where attribution was asserted vs inferred. 3) link to mint audit entry.
sam: telemetry plan: emit `auth.attribution` span for every verified token with fields: token_type, issuer, x_project (if any), resolved_project, resolution_path (x_project|api_key|fallback). emit `quota.charge` with billed_project = resolved_project.
liam: for rollout we add feature flag `billing.attribution_v1` per-org. default false. allow enable for small canary orgs. include kill-switch `billing.attribution_disable` for emergencies.
maya: finance: any reattribution will change historical numbers. plan to run replays of last 30 days for canary orgs to estimate delta before flip. ops can we get a list of orgs that use central SA patterns?
infra-bot: @maya collected list: org-342, org-501, org-900 subscribed to central-sa. export scheduled at 03:00 UTC.
aj: edge cases: what if token is reused outside scope? we should validate scope and enforce model routing. Attribution should not change enforcement semantics unless customer opts in.
sam: UX nuance: when a user inspects a token details page, show the exact resolution chain: e.g. "x_project=proj-12 (trusted issuer: sa-mint), billed_to=proj-12" or "no x_project, api_key indicates proj-7, billed_to=owner-org". small footnote on trust.
rachel: also add audit banner on project dashboards: "Some usage is attributed based on tokens minted by other orgs. Click to see provenance."
liam: implementation notes: 1) token-introspect endpoint returns canonical attributes: `sub`, `iss`, `x_project` (if mint service set), `mint_audit_id`. 2) quota router must call introspect if token opaque. 3) route decision is atomic: attribute + charge in same transaction to avoid races.
maya: operational: telemetry retention for attribution events should be 90 days initially. we may extend. also add alert when >5% requests are attributed but the org hasn't enabled rollout (possible misconfiguration).
aj: tests: unit for claim acceptance, integration test with introspect fallback, e2e with console toggle and canary org.
sam: grafana panels to build: "Attributed vs native usage" timeseries, "Top tokens reattributed", and a "Billing delta preview" heatmap. I'll open a dashboard PR after we lock metric names.
rachel: product asks for messaging: emphasise "Attribution is an opt-in billing behavior controlled by your org. When enabled, traffic minted on behalf of your projects will be charged to the project where the mint requested origin." suggest copy for console help.
deploy-bot: deploy of sa-mint v2 succeeded: rev 2026f9.
liam: ok next steps: liam + sam to spec token claim + introspect contract, aj to draft enforcement precedence, rachel to draft console copy, maya to coordinate canary list and finance replays. will reconvene after PRs.
maya: thanks everyone :thumbsup:
